title: Plan: page indexes
description: Load a folder's children from one small index file instead of every child page.

add.title: MVP: a parent reads its children's index, not the children
add.text:
Every folder gets an `index.jsonl`, one line per page inside it:

```js
{"page":{"name":"core","title":"Core","icon":"🧱","description":"…","kind":"js"}}
```

That line is exactly what `page.nav()` gives a link or a preview card. A parent shows its children from these lines and imports a child's `page.js` only when you open it.

- **Writer:** the dev server's file watcher (the one that writes `files.jsonl`).
- **Aggregate:** `GET /api/index?dir=/framework/&depth=2` — one request on the dev server; a static host fetches the folder's `index.jsonl` and each child's instead.
- **Off switch:** `Page.from_index = false` loads everything as today.

Full plan: [index-jsonl.md](/framework/core/Page/doc/index-jsonl.md)

add.title: Why: every page imports ~150 other pages
add.text:
Measured 2026-11-09, headless, main site:

| page | requests | page.js imported | bytes | quiet after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `/framework/` | 1078 | 139 | 5.7 MB | 2.4 s |
| `/framework/ai/sessions/` | 1296 | 161 | 26.6 MB | 5–17 s |
| one session page | 1322 | ~160 | 28.6 MB | 6.4 s |

The sessions grid itself reads one small file per day. The weight is the walk: each page loads its parents' children two levels deep to learn their titles, and each `page.js` pulls in its class (about 750 scripts). Plus `ai/index.json` (4 MB) fetched three or four times by the side rail.

Script: [measure.mjs](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/09/spawned/mastermind-page-index/measure.mjs)

add.title: Later: snapshots, search, mentions
add.text:
- **Snapshot vs log:** a page with thousands of lines keeps its current state beside its log, so opening it reads one line. The index line is the smallest snapshot.
- **One file:** `files.jsonl`'s file lines move into `index.jsonl`, then `files.jsonl` retires (a scripted move).
- **Cheap search, autocomplete, mentions:** all look names up in the index.
- **Exact fields:** the browser reports a page's real `nav()` when it loads one, so the index stops guessing.
